questions.solution_text:
$\tan x = -\sqrt{3}$
Reference angle: $x_{\text{ref}} = \tan^{-1}(\sqrt{3}) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$
$\tan x < 0$, so solutions lie in Quadrant 2 and Quadrant 4.
In $[-\pi, \pi]$:
Quadrant 4: $x = -\dfrac{\pi}{3}$
Quadrant 2: $x = \pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$
$x = -\dfrac{\pi}{3}, \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$

questions.solution_text:
$\sin x = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$
Reference angle: $x_{\text{ref}} = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$
$\sin x > 0$, so $x$ is in Quadrant 1 or Quadrant 2.
Quadrant 1: $x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$
Quadrant 2: $x = \pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$
$x = \dfrac{\pi}{3}, \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$

questions.solution_text:
$\sin\theta = 0$
On the unit circle, the $y$-coordinate is $0$ at the horizontal axis ($0^{\circ}$ and $180^{\circ}$).
Since $360^{\circ}$ is excluded by the domain $0^{\circ} \le \theta < 360^{\circ}$, the solutions are:
$\theta = 0^{\circ}, 180^{\circ}$

questions.solution_text:
$\cos x = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
Reference angle: $x_{\text{ref}} = \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$
$\cos x < 0$, so solutions lie in Quadrant 2 and Quadrant 3.
In $[-\pi, \pi]$:
Quadrant 2: $x = \pi - \dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$
Quadrant 3: $x = -\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{4} = -\dfrac{3\pi}{4}$
$x = -\dfrac{3\pi}{4}, \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$

questions.solution_text:
$2\sin x + \sqrt{3} = 0$
$2\sin x = -\sqrt{3}$
$\sin x = -\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$
Reference angle: $x_{\text{ref}} = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$
$\sin x < 0$, so $x$ is in Quadrant 3 or Quadrant 4.
Quadrant 3: $x = \pi + \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{4\pi}{3}$
Quadrant 4: $x = 2\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{5\pi}{3}$
$x = \dfrac{4\pi}{3}, \dfrac{5\pi}{3}$

questions.solution_text:
$\cot\theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

questions.solution_text:
$\sin\theta = -0.6$
Reference angle: $\theta_{\text{ref}} = \sin^{-1}(0.6) \approx 36.87^{\circ} \approx 37^{\circ}$
$\sin\theta < 0$, so $\theta$ is in Quadrant 3 or Quadrant 4.
Quadrant 3: $\theta = 180^{\circ} + 37^{\circ} = 217^{\circ}$
Quadrant 4: $\theta = 360^{\circ} - 37^{\circ} = 323^{\circ}$
$\theta = 217^{\circ}, 323^{\circ}$

questions.solution_text:
$\sin\theta = \dfrac{1}{2}$
Reference angle: $\theta_{\text{ref}} = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = 30^{\circ}$
$\sin\theta > 0$, so $\theta$ is in Quadrant 1 or Quadrant 2.
First revolution $[0^{\circ}, 360^{\circ}]$:
Quadrant 1: $\theta = 30^{\circ}$
Quadrant 2: $\theta = 180^{\circ} - 30^{\circ} = 150^{\circ}$
Second revolution $[360^{\circ}, 720^{\circ}]$ (adding $360^{\circ}$):
$\theta = 30^{\circ} + 360^{\circ} = 390^{\circ}$
$\theta = 150^{\circ} + 360^{\circ} = 510^{\circ}$
$\theta = 30^{\circ}, 150^{\circ}, 390^{\circ}, 510^{\circ}$
